report:
Fresh review of project_isolation's complete claim, ten ordinary implementation entries and five ordinary tests. No TODO/N/A evidence. This is source/assertion inspection, with no source edits or fresh build/test execution. Initial whole-file captures contain the relevant helper implementations; no uncaptured implementation is used as evidence here.

Project and caller independence: compile/mod.rs creates a new tempfile directory per prepare, writes the supplied validated fixture paths there and generates a standalone package manifest with an explicit empty [workspace]. It opens SageHost using that directory. rustc.rs executes the pinned compiler with current_dir set to the same project and explicitly compiles src/lib.rs as --crate-type lib, without --test or feature flags. The generated manifest contains no features or dependencies. sage-host metadata.rs runs cargo metadata in the supplied project directory and selects its ordinary library target, so the caller's directory/default workspace members do not select the fixture. Driver.rs constructs its own metadata stub and provider instance, loads that package's text files and initializes a new Database. db.rs with_proxy_and_cfgs creates fresh storage, source map and logs for each host. Same-named files/items in successive fixtures cannot reuse a previous fixture's database or source contents.

Ordinary-library configuration: metadata.rs obtains target cfg values from rustc --print cfg and the generated package's resolved enabled features. The fixture manifest defines none; the driver therefore adds no feature predicates, and neither fixture compiler nor metadata compiler requests test compilation. db.rs stores the known cfg list as a Salsa input. parse/attrs.rs evaluates cfg predicates against it, including all/any/not and feature key-value forms. parse/mod.rs applies cfg before creating enabled top-level item identities, and parse/items.rs applies the same gate for associated items; excluded modules are not loaded and excluded erroneous bodies are not checked. No enclosing test-process cfg leaks into that explicit configuration.

Deterministic logical paths: driver.rs registers package inputs relative to the selected target source directory. source.rs normalizes logical paths, including parent components needed for supported explicit module paths. parse/items.rs resolves modules from those logical names. observe.rs emits fixture-relative src/ paths rather than materialization-directory paths. rustc.rs matches structured diagnostic locations against the fixture map. These mechanisms establish source path isolation; the shared query-projection test additionally checks stable externally observable query output across independent hosts, without this review claiming a separate exhaustive query-projection audit.

All five tests: cold_queries_are_stable_across_isolated_projects prepares identical source in two fresh projects, asserts equal query text, requires executed/body evidence and rejects /tmp/ and Id( tokens. configuration_selects_items_before_checking combines all(not(test),not(feature)), any() exclusion of a nonexistent module, and associated cfg(test)/not(test) functions; an included impl method calls the enabled function, while excluded bodies would be ill-typed. fixtures_ignore_caller_directory_and_workspace_defaults launches this test executable in two child processes with updating disabled: one from an unrelated directory and another from a separate workspace whose default crate contains compile_error. Each child runs two fixtures with identical logical filenames/item names but different literal/type expectations (u16 and bool), and the parent requires process success and '1 passed' to exclude accidentally selecting no tests. This directly exercises caller-directory/default-member independence, fresh source isolation and stable snapshot paths. ordinary_library_disables_test_configuration and ordinary_library_disables_unselected_features each include an ill-typed body behind the forbidden cfg and require normal fixture success. Together these verify the two compilers see ordinary-library configuration rather than the enclosing test harness configuration. All ten implementation associations and each claim qualification are accounted for; no concrete defect or requested edit found.
